attempts.summary: Restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only, by creating opsadmin and writing /etc/cron.allow (root, opsadmin), removing the stray empty /etc/cron.deny to avoid ambiguity. Verified via crontab invocations run as each user (not root -u, which bypasses the allow list) that root and opsadmin can create/list crontabs while other users are denied with the expected cronie message. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy cron state, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until the node reconnected, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified crond is active and the allow/deny behavior persisted after reboot. All test users/crontabs created for verification were cleaned up.
